note: Relationship-driven event marketing building blocks: the fit test, anchor criteria, invite skeletons, the +1 activation loop, outreach sequences, room-design moves, post-event follow-up touches, warm-intro rules and scripts, lifecycle triggers, and the anti-pattern list. This bank is authored, not measured — the channel-effectiveness ranking and lifecycle-trigger conversion claims circulating with this system are a relationship-intelligence vendor's own framework and agents must not present them as proven. A fuller playbook lives in the shared skills shelf as the event-marketing-gtm skill. Hard rules that travel with every row: anchors come from real existing relationships only (a cold contact framed as a trusted host connection is misrepresentation), scarcity lines like a-couple-of-spots-left are used only when literally true, guest network analysis stays within publicly visible LinkedIn data and platform terms, and AI-drafted messages are human-reviewed before sending. Slots are UPPERCASE so an unfilled template trips the placeholder check in src/lib/services/deliverables/acceptance-contracts.ts.

fitTest.signal: the ICP already attends breakfasts, roundtables, and dinners in the space; strong indicator: they post about events on LinkedIn
the deal cycle is weeks to months — long enough for a relationship formed at an event to develop before it needs to convert
the ICP is geographically dispersed; one city event reaches a sliver of a multi-country market
no structured follow-up system exists; an event without one generates goodwill with no revenue attached
the fill plan is cold email or cold DMs — that is cold outreach with an event wrapper and a catering bill

principles.detail: the first 10-15 attendees set the gravitational pull of the event; the wrong ones cannot be fixed afterwards

principles.principle: every registrant is a distribution channel
principles.detail: each confirmed guest has a network of ICP lookalikes; activating it is the most efficient fill strategy available
a full room is a vanity metric; a room of connected people being actively introduced is a pipeline environment - 20 matched attendees out-produce 80 random ones

anchorCriteria.detail: decision-makers matching the ICP exactly, senior enough that peers want to share the room; someone who brings people below their level is just another attendee
the strongest anchor is the person whose LinkedIn network is mostly relevant, active ICP lookalikes - check the connections before inviting, not after
existing clients with results, then active partners, then strong warm relationships, then warm intros from those groups; cold anchors have no credibility to lend and do not work

inviteSkeletons.template:
Hey [FIRST NAME] - putting together a small [EVENT FORMAT] for [ICP ROLE] in [CITY] on [DATE]. About [SEAT COUNT] people, all [ICP SEGMENT] leaders. You came to mind given what you're building at [COMPANY].

No agenda, no pitching - just a focused conversation with relevant people. Would love to have you there. Around?
inviteSkeletons.why: personal, specific, exclusive; references their relevance, not yours; zero pressure

inviteSkeletons.template:
Subject: Quick invite - [EVENT NAME]

Hi [FIRST NAME],
[MUTUAL CONTACT] said you'd be someone worth having in the room. We're hosting a private [EVENT FORMAT] for [ICP ROLE] in [CITY] on [DATE] - around [SEAT COUNT] people, all [ICP SEGMENT], focused on [RELEVANT TOPIC]. Given what you're working on at [COMPANY], I think you'd find it genuinely useful. Worth joining us?
inviteSkeletons.why: credibility transfers from the mutual contact; specificity makes the invite feel earned

inviteSkeletons.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - running another edition of [EVENT NAME] on [DATE]. The last one was genuinely useful - [SPECIFIC THING THAT HAPPENED]. Keeping it to [SEAT COUNT] people this time, all [ICP SEGMENT]. Would love to have you back - free?
inviteSkeletons.why: the relationship is already earned; a specific callback to the last event is proof without bragging

inviteRules.rule: short and specific - a personal invite, never a newsletter
reference the relationship or the mutual connection directly; never pretend a warm invite is cold or vice versa
describe the room, not the agenda - who will be there is the pitch
make the invitee feel selected, not solicited
one clear ask at the end; start anchor outreach 6-8 weeks out so early confirmations become social proof for the next wave

activationLoop.action: scan the confirmed guest's publicly visible LinkedIn network for ICP-fit peers
shortlist 2-3 specific names who would strengthen the room
ask the guest to bring 1-2 of them as trusted plus-ones, then repeat the loop on every new confirmation

plusOneAsks.template: Locked you in for [DATE]. We're keeping it to about [SEAT COUNT] [ICP ROLE] - all [ICP SEGMENT], genuinely curated. If there are one or two peers you'd enjoy having in the room, feel free to bring them. Totally your call - we have a couple of spots left and I'd rather fill them with people you'd vouch for.
plusOneAsks.why: lands on the warmth of a fresh yes; frames it as their choice and the room as desirable

plusOneAsks.moment: 5-7 days later if no name surfaced
plusOneAsks.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - one more thing before [DATE]. I noticed you're connected to [SPECIFIC NAME] at [THEIR COMPANY] - they look like they'd fit the room well. Would you be comfortable looping them in? No pressure either way.
plusOneAsks.why: the specific name removes the cognitive load; they only have to say yes or no

plusOneAsks.template: Hey [FIRST NAME], just locked you in for [EVENT NAME] on [DATE] - really glad you're coming. Quick thing: two spots left and I'd love to fill them with people you know. If anyone from your network would enjoy it, bring them along. No obligation - just thought I'd mention it.
plusOneAsks.why: voice feels personal and low-pressure; 15-20 seconds; warm relationships only

plusOneRules.rule: the ask comes after confirmation, never before - confirmation is the trigger
frame scarcity naturally and only when it is literally true
give the guest agency - totally-your-call framing, never obligation
the best asks name a specific person you already identified from their network
it must never read as recruitment - it is an opportunity for them to share a curated room with a peer

sequences.template: the invite skeleton for the audience (EK01-EK03)
Hey [FIRST NAME] - bumping this up. We finalise the list this week; still a spot for you if you're interested. Happy to share more details.
sequences.timing: 3-4 days after touch 1 if no reply

sequences.template: Perfect - locked in for [DATE]. I'll send details and who else is coming closer to the time. One thing: if there's a peer you'd enjoy having in the room, feel free to bring them - couple of spots left and I'd rather fill them with people you'd vouch for.
sequences.timing: after confirmation; doubles as the plus-one ask

sequences.template:
Subject: Re: Quick invite - [EVENT NAME]

Just following up - we finalise the list by [DEADLINE]. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to hear who'll be there.
sequences.timing: 5 days after touch 1 if no reply

sequences.template: 20-30 second personal invite naming the format, date, room size, and ICP mix, plus a genuine personal reason to catch up - reserved for the top 3-5 anchor targets where the relationship is warm
sequences.timing: instead of the DM sequence, never for cold contacts

roomDesign.detail: never theatre-style - it kills conversation; round tables or U-shapes under 20 people; seat ICP attendees next to people they should know but don't
open with name, company, one thing you're working on - 60 seconds per person; primes conversation and gives everyone specific follow-up targets

roomDesign.move: brief the room, don't pitch it
roomDesign.detail: 2-3 sentences on why everyone is together, then hand the room back; the host is the reason people are together, not the centre of attention
one discussion question everyone has an answer to beats a series of presentations; the conversation runs itself
one page: every attendee's name, company, role, who brought them, one context note each, the 2-3 highest-priority follow-up conversations, and one starter per priority attendee

followUpTouches.template: each attending team member logs: who they spoke to, a 2-3 sentence summary, interest level (hot/warm/cold), any agreed next step, and who follows up on which channel
followUpTouches.why: half the context is gone by morning

followUpTouches.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - really enjoyed the conversation at [EVENT NAME]. [SPECIFIC REFERENCE TO WHAT YOU DISCUSSED]. Would love to continue it - free for a quick call this week?
followUpTouches.why: speed signals the conversation mattered; in-person warmth decays fast

followUpTouches.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - great to meet you at [EVENT NAME], glad [REFERRER NAME] brought you along. [SPECIFIC REFERENCE TO CONVERSATION]. Open to a 20-minute call this week?
followUpTouches.why: names the referrer, inheriting their credibility

followUpTouches.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - sorry we didn't get to connect at [EVENT NAME], hope all's OK. Good session - happy to share a quick summary of what came up if useful, and flexible on a better time to catch up.
followUpTouches.why: keeps a confirmed-but-absent lead warm without guilt

followUpTouches.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - wanted to say a proper thank you for bringing [PLUS ONE NAMES]. Exactly the right people for the room, and the conversations were great. We'll follow up with them properly - really appreciate it.
followUpTouches.why: anchors staked credibility; visibility into what happened after turns one-time referrers into repeat ones

followUpTouches.timing: while the event is warm, within 72 hours
followUpTouches.template: Hey [FIRST NAME] - really enjoyed the conversation at [EVENT NAME]. Quick question while the context is fresh - I noticed you're connected to [SPECIFIC NAME] at [THEIR COMPANY]. They look like a relevant person for us to know. Would you be comfortable making a quick intro? Happy to write the message so it's zero effort on your end.
followUpTouches.why: post-event goodwill is at its peak; the specific name plus zero-friction offer makes yes easy

introRules.detail: never ask if they know anyone who might be a fit - that outsources your research; ask for one named person so the answer is yes or no
provide a ready-to-forward intro email, a copyable short message, and a 2-line pitch; for complex products keep the narrative in your intro text rather than delegating the explanation
feel-free-to-mention-my-name converts poorly; a 3-way email or group message converts far better; if passive is all they'll do, act within the hour
a C-level intro at a strategic account is a single ask; mid-level profiles at most 1-2; over-asking signals opportunism

introScripts.template:
Subject: Introduction - [YOUR NAME] and [PROSPECT NAME]

Hi [PROSPECT NAME],
Wanted to introduce you to [YOUR NAME] at [YOUR COMPANY]. They work with [ICP DESCRIPTION] on [PROBLEM YOU SOLVE]. Given what you're building at [PROSPECT COMPANY], thought it was worth connecting you. I'll leave it to you both from here.
[REFERRER NAME]
introScripts.why: short, neutral, no overselling - the referrer's credibility beats any pitch you could write

introScripts.template: Hey [ANCHOR NAME] - really glad you brought [PLUS ONE NAME] yesterday, great conversation. One more thing while the context is fresh - I noticed [PLUS ONE NAME] is connected to [SPECIFIC NAME] at [THEIR COMPANY], who looks relevant for us. Would you be comfortable asking [PLUS ONE NAME] to make a quick intro? I can write the message if that helps.
introScripts.why: one event yields multiple intro layers when you activate the networks of the people in the room, not just the people themselves

introScripts.template: three checkpoints to the referrer: when the meeting books, after the first call (how it went, interest level, next steps), and at end of cycle win or lose with genuine thanks
introScripts.why: a referrer who hears nothing after an intro never makes another one

lifecycleTriggers.trigger: before or after in-person meetings and events - the post-event window this bank is built around

channelHierarchyClaim: the source vendor ranks intro-ask channels in-person, then live call or video, then written - directionally sensible, but a vendor framework, not measured data; a post-event message counts as a continuation of in-person contact rather than a cold written ask
compensationRule: credibility outweighs incentive in B2B; if rewarding referrers, recognise effort over time - a small acknowledgement when the first meeting books and a meaningful reward at signature, never a single thank-you months later at close

antiPatterns.why: an invite that looks sent to 500 people gets treated like it was; personalise the first line at minimum and reference the relationship
an-event-for-GTM-leaders says nothing; a breakfast for 15 named-segment leaders in a named city is the whole pitch - specificity is the hook
no case studies, features, or ROI claims; the invite has one job - make them want to be in the room
one off-ICP guest dilutes the peer-room dynamic; qualification bar: would you cold-email this person your core offer
a calendar invite plus showing up is venue hire; message every confirmed guest 5-7 days out naming 2-3 people they should meet and why

antiPatterns.pattern: no intro architecture inside the event
antiPatterns.why: a client and their lookalike prospect standing metres apart un-introduced is pipeline left on the table; map introductions beforehand and physically make them

antiPatterns.pattern: asking for pipeline at the event
antiPatterns.why: pitching in the room destroys the trust the room exists to build; the event is never the ask - the 24-48 hour follow-up is

antiPatterns.pattern: building the follow-up system after the event
antiPatterns.why: warm conversations decay in about 72 hours while you improvise; decide who follows up with whom, saying what, on which channel, by when - before doors open
no credibility with their network, no reason to bring peers, may not even show; anchors come from existing clients and partners only
